subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Should OpenClaw make 150 seconds for lock-held OAuth work and 360 seconds for runtime auth the supported failure boundary, accepting a surfaced auth error and retry rather than allowing an indefinitely blocked agent lane?
rationale: The patch is a coherent implementation of one availability policy, but choosing the deadline and accepting uncancellable post-timeout provider work is a cross-provider operational contract rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Approve the bounded-recovery contract
options.body: Accept the 150s/360s deadlines and the guarded retry behavior as the supported way to recover a blocked gateway lane.

options.title: Choose a different provider policy
options.body: Keep the deadlock objective but specify different timeout, retry, or provider-specific cancellation semantics before implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded-recovery contract
recommendation.body: Accept the 150s/360s deadlines and the guarded retry behavior as the supported way to recover a blocked gateway lane.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work spans the adjacent OAuth contention and runtime credential-boundary contracts affected by this policy choice.
